summary.headline: SIS Ltd Q2 FY27: record EBITDA of 481.6 crore, up 28.1% YoY, with margin expansion in every segment.
summary.overview: SIS reported record quarterly EBITDA and profit, with EBITDA growing faster than revenue. Management said minimum-wage cost pass-through is starting to show in margins, with India segment margin up 16 bps QoQ to 5.3% and the overall margin up from 5.2% to 5.4%. International working capital worsened on one delayed large government collection, lifting group net debt-to-EBITDA to 1.24x from 1.05x. Management reiterated 15-18% overall growth guidance and a target of getting debt-to-EBITDA back to about 1x.

financial_highlights.change: From 1.05x; management attributes rise to buyback/dividend payouts of about 2,047 crore and the international delay
Expected to return to about 50-51 days in next quarter

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue of 2,144 crore (+15.7% YoY, +6% QoQ) with EBITDA margin up 16 bps QoQ to 5.3%. Management said margins rose from 5.2% to 5.4% at group level in early stages of wage pass-through.

segments.name: International (QT Solutions International / Australia)
segments.commentary: Record revenue, with EBITDA of about 72 crore (+35% YoY) and margin of 3.6%. Working capital deteriorated on one delayed large customer collection of about 120 million, which management says was collected in October.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Management said the business grew about 20% plus YoY, with EBITDA down a little QoQ due to lower grants linked to the PWM rate.

segments.name: Logistics JV (minority, not consolidated)
segments.commentary: Record revenue of about 220 crore with EBITDA margin above 17%. Share of profit now reported below the line as share of profit from joint venture; the listing was on hold due to adverse market conditions and the approval period has expired.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the margin expansion trend (5.2% to 5.4% in Q2) to continue over the next two quarters, without quantifying it.
Wage-code cost pass-through expected to lift revenue and margins; management said it has no quantified revenue uplift to give yet.
International debt days expected to normalise to about 50-51 in the next quarter; group net debt expected to decline by December.
Debt-to-EBITDA policy target of about 1x, with buybacks and dividends continuing alongside debt reduction.
Acquisitions in international business are being explored in specific areas (capability, geography, scale); no timeline given.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Fifth buyback tranche completed in the quarter, with payouts of about 2,047 crore cited as a driver of higher leverage (transcript wording unclear).
demand_pricing: Wage-code and minimum-wage cost increases are being passed through to customers; management said competitors should follow once state model rules are notified.
Australia minimum wage rises each July; pass-through happens at contract anniversaries, with bulk in July-September and October-December.
Interest cost: about 8.5% on India debt and about 7.0-7.2% on international debt (Murli Krishnan's figure of 6.5% was corrected).
Management said the company has no quantified revenue uplift from wage-code pass-through yet, only early signs in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-time labour code cost from Q3 FY26 still affecting the business, and was there a reversal in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time exceptional item was accounted for per ICAI guidance, with no further impact expected. Employee separation costs are being recovered from customers, so there is no cash flow impact. The Q4 reversal was an accounting adjustment from fair-valuing an investment, moving part of it from profit or loss to OCI.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue uplift can the wage code bring?
qa_highlights.answer: No number given. Management said early revenue benefit is visible in Q2 and guidance remains at 15-18% growth, with the margin trend expected to continue over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend and buyback policy, and the mix between them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to 700 crore has been returned since the IPO. It will keep returning cash through dividends and buybacks while investing in the business and reducing debt; no fixed split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was international working capital weaker, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June is seasonally strong for collections, but one major government customer's collection of about 120 million slipped and was received in October. International debt days should return to about 50-51 next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target debt level, and what are the interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is debt-to-EBITDA around 1x, currently 1.24x, expected to come back to 1x or below. India interest cost is about 8.5%, and international about 7.0-7.2%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Singapore business doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it grew about 20% plus YoY and orders are being renewed. EBITDA declined slightly QoQ on lower grants linked to the PWM rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions are an established strategy in international business, targeting capability, geography or scale. Target candidates are being cultivated but no timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the logistics JV be reported going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV's EBITDA will be disclosed separately in the earnings note from next quarter. It is a minority JV, so its profit share sits under share of profit from joint venture in the P&L and it is not consolidated on the balance sheet.

risks_watch: International working capital and collections: debt days at 73 and net debt rose to 256 crore; the company says this should normalise to 50-51 days next quarter.
Group leverage at 1.24x versus the stated 1x policy, with buybacks and dividends continuing.
Wage-code pass-through depends on state model rules and on competitors following; timing is staggered by contract anniversary.
Logistics listing is on hold after the approval period expired.
Founder chairman passing on 30 October 2026; leadership continuity to watch.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the wage-code tailwind, but cautious and somewhat evasive on quantifying revenue uplift and on the timing of the international working capital recovery. Management gave no numbers on the acquisition pipeline.
key_quotes: Costs are being fully passed through to customers lifting both the revenue and the rise of minimum wages.
So keeping that in that level we will also need to see that the commitment towards our shareholders

growth.why: Management held 15-18% overall growth guidance (midpoint 16.5%), backed by wage-code cost pass-through to customers, but said it has no quantified revenue uplift yet and gave no capacity additions, capex or utilisation figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated margin rose from 5.2% to 5.4% QoQ and India segment margin up 16 bps QoQ to 5.3% as minimum-wage pass-through starts; management expects the trend to continue over the next two quarters but did not quantify it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, plant, branch or fleet additions were discussed on the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance held at 15-18% (midpoint 16.5%) with Q2 India revenue up 15.7% YoY and Singapore growing about 20%+ YoY, but no volume split was given and the wage-pass-through revenue uplift is unquantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or utilisation figures were discussed; the only capital outflow cited is buyback and dividend payouts of about 2,047 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management simply reiterated 15-18% growth guidance and gave no quantified revenue uplift from wage-code pass-through, so there is no sign of a raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Group net debt-to-EBITDA rose to 1.24x from 1.05x against a 1x target, and international debt days at 73 depend on a delayed government collection that management says will normalise to 50-51 days next quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed.

rows.label: International debt days normalise to 50-51
rows.why: Debt days at 73 and international net debt of 256 crore (from 11 crore) should reverse as the approximately 120 million delayed government collection was received in October, per management.

rows.label: International acquisitions
rows.why: Management says acquisitions in capability, geography or scale are being explored and targets are being cultivated, but gave no numbers or timeline.

rows.label: Debt-to-EBITDA back to about 1x
rows.why: Leverage is 1.24x versus 1.05x last quarter; management expects group net debt to decline by December, but buybacks and dividends (about 2,047 crore cited) continue alongside debt reduction.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin expansion and the wage-code pass-through, but cautious and evasive on quantifying the revenue uplift and on the timing of international working capital recovery; analysts pushed on the wage-code revenue number, leverage and cash returns.
